newsitem.title: UK: Ford confirms UK job cuts.
newsitem.headline: Ford confirms UK job cuts.

text.p: Ford Motor Co's UK division confirmed on Thursday plans for 1,300 job cuts at its Halewood plant on Merseyside, north west England.

Ford UK said in a statement that the Halewood plant would not build the planned new model of the Escort car, which is seen being transferred to continental European factories. It did hold out the possibility of Halewood becoming the European source of a planned new vehicle, which is still only a concept at this stage.

Unions responded angrily, saying that Ford had moved to axe jobs in the UK as it was cheaper than doing so in continental Europe, and called for further negotiations. Larry Brook of the MSF Union said, "Britain is the cheapest place to dump labour -- we are fighting for the future of Halewood." Unions beleive that the European Union's "social chapter' would have made it more expensive for Ford to shed jobs on the continent.
Ford said the Halewood plant would continue to make the current Escort model through 2000.

David Gorman, its European vehicle operations manager, said, "The actions we have announced today at Halewood assembly operations give the plant a realistic future, with an exciting new vehicle in the medium term, subject to approval and performance objectives being achieved. We have had to take these steps to ensure our manned capacity is in line with our forecasts for sales."

Unions, including engineering industry union AAEU, said that a large proportion of the cars built at Halewood are sold in the UK market and therefore should continue to be made there. "We are not trying to pinch jobs from the Spaniards," said one union offical, "but we want our share."
